summary: Peak in Lemhi County on the Salmon NF; the only lookout record found is a 1924 report of a patrol camp below the summit and no summit improvements.

visit.trail_note: Unmaintained trail up the west face, then a short bushwhack to the ridge summit; the guide says FST-039 is no longer maintained.

events.note: Lookout-patrolman-smokechaser camp half a mile below the summit; no improvements on the summit

evidence.supports: 1924 lookout report: camp half a mile below summit; no summit improvements
evidence.quote: 1924: The Salmon Forest lookout report states that the lookout-patrolman-smokechaser has a camp a half mile below the summit. No improvements on the summit.

evidence.supports: Summit is the high point of a forested ridge southeast of Hoodoo Meadows in the Yellowjacket Mountains
evidence.quote: McEleny Mountain is the high point on a forested ridge located southeast of Hoodoo Meadows in the Yellowjacket Mountains.

evidence.supports: Unmaintained trail on west face, short bushwhack to ridgeline summit
evidence.quote: It can be reached by an unmaintained trail on the west face and a short bushwhack to the ridgeline summit.
The summit offers beautiful views of the surrounding area.

evidence.supports: Approach by forest roads from Panther Creek Road to Hoodoo Meadows trailhead
evidence.quote: From Panther Creek Road, drive west up FSR-112/Porphry Creek Road

evidence.supports: Road ends at the south end of Hoodoo Meadows, where the trailhead is
evidence.quote: At 6.4 miles, reach the end of the road at the south end of Hoodoo Meadows.

notes_for_editor: Lemhi County and Salmon NF are supported by the Idaho Forest Lookouts page. The 1924 entry is the only lookout evidence; nothing read says a structure was built, when, or what became of it. firelookout.org's Idaho list has no McEleny entry, and the Bing Young 1982 overview of Salmon NF lookouts does not name it (not cited). The brief coordinates (45.02881, -114.54453) are about 3 km from the guide's trailhead at 45 03'12"N, 114 33'46"W; not corrected. Do not confuse with Blue Nose (Lemhi, standing) or Taylor Mountain.
